summary: This video demonstrates how to use Quiver Quant and Alpaca paper trading with Claude to automate stock trades. It shows setting up accounts, connecting MCP servers, placing trades, and backtesting strategies, all without real money.

claims.text: Claude can place stock trades via a single prompt using Quiver Quant and Alpaca paper trading.
claims.evidence_quote: Claude can place trades for you in a single prompt, and you do not have to do any manual work.

claims.text: Paper trading with Alpaca simulates real trading without using real money.
claims.evidence_quote: We will create a paper trading account with Alpaca, which simulates what it is like to trade with real money and observe how it's doing over time.

claims.text: API keys act like passwords and should be kept private to prevent unauthorized trades.
claims.evidence_quote: API keys act a lot like a password, and so if anybody gets access to that password, they might be able to have access to your account and make trades on your behalf.

claims.text: The free account method does not allow automatic rebalancing; you must manually ask Claude to update holdings.
claims.evidence_quote: The one downside to using the MCP servers and just a free account is that you cannot set some sort of schedule for the algorithm to rerun and update your holdings.

claims.text: The video demonstrates placing an order for one share of Apple via Claude.
claims.evidence_quote: The next thing that we're gonna test out is purchasing one share of Apple.

claims.text: The backtest used the Pelosi strategy and compared its performance to the market.
claims.evidence_quote: it looks like it grabbed up the Pelosi strategy, um, how that performed over time and how that performed in comparison to the market.

claims.text: Quiver strategies can be backtested to see historical performance.
claims.evidence_quote: you can back test those same strategies to see how they've performed in the past.

claims.text: The setup for Alpaca is quick and free.
claims.evidence_quote: setup is really quick, and it's also free.

claims.text: The video instructs to use Quiver's data and Alpaca's data for backtesting to ensure accuracy.
claims.evidence_quote: we really wanna stick to Quiver's data and Alpaca's data 'cause we know we can rely on those to be true.
